author: Shannon Brown
title: When a security-system outage becomes a business-risk decision
summary: The critical question is what the business can safely continue while its picture is incomplete.
judgment: Treat a loss of security visibility as a business-risk decision when the remaining controls can no longer support the activity being protected.
assumptions: A fictional organization has a partial monitoring outage; no immediate life-safety emergency is established.
alternatives: Continue normally if independent controls preserve the required assurance; suspend activity if the consequence cannot be contained.
indicators: Independent verification fails, the affected activity becomes more consequential, or a promised compensating control cannot be sustained.

author: Shannon Brown
title: What an executive brief must say before the picture is complete
summary: Useful uncertainty tells a decision-maker what can be done now—and what evidence would change the call.
judgment: An incomplete picture can support a sound decision when the brief separates what is observed, what is inferred, and what must be decided before better information arrives.
assumptions: A decision has a real time constraint and a named owner; the example does not describe a live incident.
alternatives: Delay the recommendation when the decision is reversible and the next evidence is both timely and consequential.
indicators: A critical assumption fails, credible contrary reporting arrives, the decision window changes, or the proposed treatment becomes infeasible.
